lessons.title: The Drop
lessons.summary: Gravity makes falling things speed up.

steps.title: Gravity speeds things up
steps.text: When you drop a ball, it starts slow and falls faster and faster. That's gravity. So the gaps between your drawings get bigger each frame: small at the top, big at the bottom.

steps.title: Drop it
steps.text: Draw the ball falling. Make each gap bigger than the one before.
steps.hint: Tiny gap at the top, biggest gap at the bottom.

quiz.question: When a ball falls, its drawings should be...
choices: Close together at the top, far apart at the bottom
Far apart at the top, close at the bottom
quiz.explain: Gravity makes it faster as it falls, so the gaps grow.

steps.title: Up, down, up
steps.text: A bounce is a fall and a rise. Going up, the ball slows down until it stops at the top for a moment. Coming down, it speeds up until it hits the ground. So the drawings bunch up at the top and spread out near the ground.

steps.title: Moving forward
steps.text: If the ball also moves sideways, the sideways spacing stays even while the up-and-down spacing follows gravity. Together they make an arc, like the orange path.

steps.title: One bounce
steps.text: Draw a whole bounce in place: ground, rising, top, falling. Frame 6 leads back to frame 1.
steps.hint: The two drawings near the top are close together. Near the ground they're far apart.

quiz.question: Where does a bouncing ball move slowest?
choices: At the top of the bounce
Just before it hits the ground
quiz.explain: At the top it stops going up and starts coming down, so it's slowest there.

steps.title: Squish on impact
steps.text: Now add squash and stretch. Just before and after it hits the ground, the ball is moving fastest, so it stretches along its path. On the frame it touches the ground, it squashes flat. At the top it's round.

steps.title: Keep the volume
steps.text: A squashed ball gets wider. A stretched ball gets thinner. It always keeps the same amount of ball, or it will look like it's growing and shrinking.

steps.title: Three key drawings
steps.text: Draw the ball stretched as it falls, squashed on the ground, then stretched as it shoots back up.
steps.hint: Tall and thin, then short and wide, then tall and thin again.

quiz.question: When is the ball stretched the most?
choices: When it's moving fastest, near the ground
quiz.explain: Speed causes stretch, and the ball is fastest near the ground.

lessons.title: Losing Energy
lessons.summary: Each bounce is lower than the last.

steps.title: Smaller and smaller
steps.text: A real ball loses a little energy every time it hits the ground, so each bounce is lower and shorter than the one before, until it rolls to a stop.

steps.title: Trace the bounce path
steps.text: Trace the path the ball takes. Each hump is lower than the last.
steps.hint: Go over the humps one at a time, touching the ground between them.

quiz.question: Each bounce should be...
choices: Lower and shorter than the one before
quiz.explain: The ball loses energy each time it lands.

quiz.question: Why do the bounces get lower?
choices: The ball loses some energy every time it hits
quiz.explain: Some energy turns into sound and squish each time it hits the ground.

steps.title: Heavy or light?
steps.text: A heavy bowling ball drops hard, hardly bounces and doesn't squash. A light beach ball drifts down, squashes a lot and bounces high and slow. Same shape, different weight, all shown with timing.

quiz.question: Which ball is the heavy bowling ball?
quiz.explain: It falls hard, lands with a thud and barely bounces.

steps.title: Heavy drop
steps.text: Draw the bowling ball falling fast. The gaps grow quickly.
steps.hint: Small gap, bigger gap, biggest gap.

quiz.question: A light beach ball should...
choices: Bounce high and float down slowly
quiz.explain: Air slows light things down, so they float.
